- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment shows rising optimism (e.g., >0.6 over 3–5 days), model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in early days of forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead); apply 1–2% upward bias for first 3 days of 30d forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral or declining (0.0–0.3), model often overcorrects downward; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to prevent premature sell-off.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >1.5% from 15d moving average, apply mean reversion correction: pull forecast toward 15d MA by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.7), model misreads momentum; reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% in such regimes.
